# dggbal

> Balances a pair of general real matrices (A, B).

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dggbal from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dggbal';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dggbal(
    order,
    job,
    N,
    A, LDA,
    B, LDB,
    ilo,
    ihi,
    LSCALE, strideLSCALE,
    RSCALE, strideRSCALE,
    WORK
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `job` | `"none" \| "permute" \| "scale" \| "both"` | `'none'`, `'permute'`, `'scale'`, or `'both'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrices<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · First real matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of A<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Second real matrix |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of B<br>Requires `LDB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `ilo` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `ilo` |
| `ihi` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): iLO and IHI are set to integers such that on exit A(i,j) = 0 and B(i,j) = 0 if i > j and j = 1,...,ILO-1 or i = IHI+1,...,N |
| `LSCALE` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Left scaling factors |
| ↳ `strideLSCALE` | `integer` | Stride for LSCALE |
| `RSCALE` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Right scaling factors |
| ↳ `strideRSCALE` | `integer` | Stride for RSCALE |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null` | **out** · Workspace array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `job`: Specifies the operations to be performed on A and B:

  -   `= 'N'`: none:  simply set `ILO = 1`, `IHI = N`, `LSCALE(I) = 1.0` and `RSCALE(I) = 1.0` for $i = 1$,...,N.
  -   `= 'P'`: permute only;
  -   `= 'S'`: scale only;
  -   `= 'B'`: both permute and scale.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the input matrix A. On exit, A is overwritten by the balanced matrix. If `JOB = 'N'`, A is not referenced.
- `B`: On entry, the input matrix B. On exit, B is overwritten by the balanced matrix. If `JOB = 'N'`, B is not referenced.
- `ihi`: `ILO` and `IHI` are set to integers such that on exit $A(i,j) = 0$ and $B(i,j) = 0$ if $i > j$ and $j = 1$,...,`ILO`-1 or $i = \mathrm{IHI}+1$,...,N. If `JOB = 'N'` or 'S', `ILO = 1` and `IHI = N`.
- `LSCALE`: Details of the permutations and scaling factors applied to the left side of A and B. If P(j) is the index of the row interchanged with row j, and D(j) is the scaling factor applied to row j, then

  ```text
  LSCALE(j) = P(j)    for J = 1,...,ILO-1
            = D(j)    for J = ILO,...,IHI
            = P(j)    for J = IHI+1,...,N.
  ```

  The order in which the interchanges are made is N to `IHI`+1, then 1 to `ILO`-1.
- `RSCALE`: Details of the permutations and scaling factors applied to the right side of A and B. If P(j) is the index of the column interchanged with column j, and D(j) is the scaling factor applied to column j, then

  ```text
  LSCALE(j) = P(j)    for J = 1,...,ILO-1
            = D(j)    for J = ILO,...,IHI
            = P(j)    for J = IHI+1,...,N.
  ```

  The order in which the interchanges are made is N to `IHI`+1, then 1 to `ILO`-1.
- `WORK`: lwork must be at least max(1,6\*N) when `JOB = 'S'` or 'B', and at least 1 when `JOB = 'N'` or 'P'.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "both", "none", "permute", "scale"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dggbal.ndarray(
    job,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    ilo,
    ihi,
    LSCALE, strideLSCALE, offsetLSCALE,
    RSCALE, strideRSCALE, offsetRSCALE,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `job` | `"none" \| "permute" \| "scale" \| "both"` | `'none'`, `'permute'`, `'scale'`, or `'both'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrices A and B<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · First real matrix (modified in-place) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Second real matrix (modified in-place) |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of B |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of B |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for B |
| `ilo` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `ilo` |
| `ihi` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): iLO and IHI are set to integers such that on exit A(i,j) = 0 and B(i,j) = 0 if i > j and j = 1,...,ILO-1 or i = IHI+1,...,N |
| `LSCALE` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Left scaling/permutation factors (length N) |
| ↳ `strideLSCALE` | `integer` | Stride for LSCALE |
| ↳ `offsetLSCALE` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for LSCALE |
| `RSCALE` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Right scaling/permutation factors (length N) |
| ↳ `strideRSCALE` | `integer` | Stride for RSCALE |
| ↳ `offsetRSCALE` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for RSCALE |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Workspace array (length >= 6\*N) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `job`: Specifies the operations to be performed on A and B:

  -   `= 'N'`: none:  simply set `ILO = 1`, `IHI = N`, `LSCALE(I) = 1.0` and `RSCALE(I) = 1.0` for $i = 1$,...,N.
  -   `= 'P'`: permute only;
  -   `= 'S'`: scale only;
  -   `= 'B'`: both permute and scale.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the input matrix A. On exit, A is overwritten by the balanced matrix. If `JOB = 'N'`, A is not referenced.
- `B`: On entry, the input matrix B. On exit, B is overwritten by the balanced matrix. If `JOB = 'N'`, B is not referenced.
- `ihi`: `ILO` and `IHI` are set to integers such that on exit $A(i,j) = 0$ and $B(i,j) = 0$ if $i > j$ and $j = 1$,...,`ILO`-1 or $i = \mathrm{IHI}+1$,...,N. If `JOB = 'N'` or 'S', `ILO = 1` and `IHI = N`.
- `LSCALE`: Details of the permutations and scaling factors applied to the left side of A and B. If P(j) is the index of the row interchanged with row j, and D(j) is the scaling factor applied to row j, then

  ```text
  LSCALE(j) = P(j)    for J = 1,...,ILO-1
            = D(j)    for J = ILO,...,IHI
            = P(j)    for J = IHI+1,...,N.
  ```

  The order in which the interchanges are made is N to `IHI`+1, then 1 to `ILO`-1.
- `RSCALE`: Details of the permutations and scaling factors applied to the right side of A and B. If P(j) is the index of the column interchanged with column j, and D(j) is the scaling factor applied to column j, then

  ```text
  LSCALE(j) = P(j)    for J = 1,...,ILO-1
            = D(j)    for J = ILO,...,IHI
            = P(j)    for J = IHI+1,...,N.
  ```

  The order in which the interchanges are made is N to `IHI`+1, then 1 to `ILO`-1.
- `WORK`: lwork must be at least max(1,6\*N) when `JOB = 'S'` or 'B', and at least 1 when `JOB = 'N'` or 'P'.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "both", "none", "permute", "scale"
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0` or `N === 1`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dggbal from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dggbal';

const ilo = new Int32Array( 1 );
const ihi = new Int32Array( 1 );

const A = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );
const B = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] );
const LSCALE = new Float64Array( 2 );
const RSCALE = new Float64Array( 2 );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 12 );

const result = dggbal.ndarray( 'both', 2, A, 1, 2, 0, B, 1, 2, 0, ilo, ihi, LSCALE, 1, 0, RSCALE, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', result ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'ilo:', ilo[ 0 ] );   // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'ihi:', ihi[ 0 ] );   // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DGGBAL`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DGGBAL balances a pair of general real matrices (A,B). This involves, first, permuting A and B by similarity transformations to isolate eigenvalues in the first 1 to `ILO`\$-\$1 and last `IHI`+1 to N elements on the diagonal; and second, applying a diagonal similarity transformation to rows and columns `ILO` to `IHI` to make the rows and columns as close in norm as possible. Both steps are optional.

Balancing may reduce the 1-norm of the matrices, and improve the accuracy of the computed eigenvalues and/or eigenvectors in the generalized eigenvalue problem $A \, x = \lambda \, B \, x$.

### Further Details

See R.C. WARD, Balancing the generalized eigenvalue problem,

SIAM J. Sci. Stat. Comp. 2 (1981), 141-152.

</section>
